chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the forearm when it is struck and the ulna (zen) breaks from it. He said: If the palm dries out and all the fingers of the hand become paralyzed, then in it is two-thirds of the blood money of the hand. And if some of the fingers become paralyzed and some remain, then in each paralyzed finger is two-thirds of its blood money. He said: And the same ruling applies to the leg and the foot when the fingers of the foot become paralyzed.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money (financial compensation for bodily injury)
key_terms.الزَّنْد: Ulna (the larger bone of the forearm)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for blood money compensation when fingers or toes become paralyzed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfarayini’s chain in al-Isfabar establishes the precise jurisprudential calculation for 'shall' (paralysis) in the limbs, distinguishing between total and partial loss of function. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of applying proportional logic to bodily injuries, where the value of a finger is derived from the whole hand, ensuring equitable compensation in cases of physical disability.
